$ go test  # used-fewer-a
    the lift import is used by ./b, and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    the lifts parse and resolve are used by ./b on the path testdata/export/ → import → parse and past it, and ., which owns them, doesn't run them over testdata/export/, so no package writes their cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past them are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does. In ., register the corpus type of testdata/export/, and give import to hypercase.Own, so . runs them over testdata/export/ too. If . registers them already, or ./b doesn't reach them from testdata/export/, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks/paths
FAIL
[exit 1]
